block.abstand.langsam: It arrived {min} minutes after its predecessor; the network aims for ten.
block.abstand.normal: It arrived {min} minutes after its predecessor — close to the ten minutes the network aims for.
block.abstand.rueckwaerts: Its timestamp lies {min} minutes BEFORE its predecessor's. That is allowed: a block only has to be newer than the median of the eleven blocks before it.
block.abstand.schnell: It arrived just {min} minutes after its predecessor, faster than the ten minutes the network aims for.
block.abstand.sofort: It followed its predecessor after only {min} minutes — someone got lucky.
block.arbeit: At a difficulty of {diff}, an average of {w} {einheit} had to be hashed to find it.
block.band.hilfe: Each column is the fee rate below which that share of the block's weight sits. The scale ends at the 90th percentile, so a single expensive transaction cannot flatten all the others; it is named above instead.
block.bestaetigt: {n} blocks have been stacked on top of it since — it counts as final.
block.bewegt: Its transactions moved {btc} BTC in total, change included.
block.epoche: It belongs to reward epoch {e}. The next halving falls on block {h}, {n} blocks away — roughly {tage} days at ten minutes per block.
block.fenster: Every comparison above refers to the {n} preceding blocks — {std} hours of chain.
block.frisch: Only {n} blocks sit on top of it so far; six is the usual threshold for calling a payment final.
block.fuellung.halb: Half empty — there was no real competition for space here.
block.fuellung.leer: Mostly empty. Either the mempool was worked off or the miner did not fill it.
block.fuellung.randvoll: Space was the binding constraint: nothing more would have fitted in.
block.fuellung.voll: Nearly full — the mempool had more to offer than fitted in.
block.gebuehrenanteil: Fees made up {p}% of that income.
block.guenstigste: The cheapest transaction in it paid {r} sat/vB.

block.leer: Apart from the coinbase it held no transaction at all — an empty block.

block.median_rate: Half of the block's weight paid more than {r} sat/vB, the other half less.
block.nach_halbierung: After the next halving, those same fees would be {p}% of it.
block.nf.form: “{eingabe}” is neither a block height nor a block hash.

block.spitze: Nothing sits on top of it yet: this is the tip of the chain.

block.urteil.tiefster: No block among the last {n} was lower.

block.utxo.bytes_weniger: Every full node on earth now carries {kb} kB less because of it.
block.utxo.gleich: It created {aus} outputs and spent exactly as many — the UTXO set is the same size as before.
block.utxo.schrumpfung: It created {aus} outputs, spent {ein}, and shrank the UTXO set by {d} — this block tidied up.
block.utxo.wachstum: It created {aus} outputs, spent {ein}, and let the UTXO set grow by only {d}.

tx.band.andrang: Where its fee rate sits among what the queue currently costs
tx.band.block: Where its fee rate sat among the other transactions in its block
tx.chunk.none: this node does not report chunks
tx.f.ahnen: It hangs off {n} unconfirmed ancestors. What counts for a miner is not its own fee but the whole chain's: {rate} sat/vB.
tx.f.ahnen_1: It hangs off one unconfirmed ancestor. What counts for a miner is not its own fee but the whole chain's: {rate} sat/vB.
tx.f.alle_weg: All {n} outputs have already been spent again.
tx.f.antisniping: Its locktime is set to block {h} — the height that was current when it was signed. That is how wallets stop a miner from rewriting the last few blocks just to grab its fee.
tx.f.bestaetigt_1: Confirmed once, in block {h}. A single confirmation can still be undone by a chain reorganisation.
tx.f.chunk: Miners do not weigh it on its own: it sits in a mining chunk of {n} transactions paying {rate} sat/vB together. That chunk is what a block takes whole or leaves whole.
tx.f.cluster: It belongs to a cluster of {n} unconfirmed transactions that depend on one another.
tx.f.coinbase: This transaction created new bitcoin — it is the reward for block {h}.
tx.f.coinbase_reif: Its outputs stay locked for another {n} blocks; only then can they be spent.
tx.f.coinbase_tag: The miner wrote “{text}” into its input.
tx.f.coinbase_teile: Of that reward, {sub} BTC is freshly minted; {geb} BTC are fees from the {n} other transactions in the block.
tx.f.coinbase_teile_kurz: Of that reward, {sub} BTC is freshly minted and {geb} BTC are fees from the rest of the block.
tx.f.gebuehr_anteil: The fee amounts to {p}% of the value moved.
tx.f.gross: At {v} vbytes it takes up {p}% of an entire block.
tx.f.kein_segwit: It does not use SegWit, so it pays full price for every byte of signature.
tx.f.keine_prevouts: The input amounts are missing: this node cannot look up the transactions they came from, because it keeps no transaction index or has been pruned. Fee and input total therefore stay open.
tx.f.nachfahren: {n} unconfirmed descendants hang off it; together they pay {rate} sat/vB and are mined together.
tx.f.nachfahren_1: One unconfirmed descendant hangs off it; together they pay {rate} sat/vB and are mined together.
tx.f.offen: It is not in a block yet.
tx.f.opreturn: One output carries no payment but {b} bytes of data written into the blockchain.
tx.f.opreturn_text: One output carries no payment but {b} bytes of data: {text}
tx.f.perzentil_hoch: At {rate} sat/vB it paid more than nine out of ten transactions in its block.
tx.f.perzentil_mitte: At {rate} sat/vB it sat in the middle of its block, whose median was {median} sat/vB.
tx.f.perzentil_niedrig: At {rate} sat/vB it paid less than nine out of ten transactions in its block — it got in cheaply.
tx.f.raus_geflogen: It sits close to the mempool's minimum fee ({min} sat/vB). If traffic rises, it is among the first to be evicted.
tx.f.rbf_ererbt: It does not signal replaceability itself, but it hangs off an unconfirmed ancestor that does — so it can be replaced anyway.
tx.f.rbf_ja: This transaction signals that it may be replaced.
tx.f.rbf_nein: It does not signal replaceability. Do not rely on that: many nodes now accept a replacement without the signal.
tx.f.reicht: At the current level of traffic its fee is enough for a confirmation within about {n} blocks.
tx.f.reicht_naechster: At the current level of traffic its fee is enough for the next block.
tx.f.reicht_nicht: Its fee is below every estimate this node makes — even for a wait of {n} blocks it reckons {rate} sat/vB.
tx.f.segwit: SegWit: its witness data is {b} bytes but counts as only {v} vbytes, saving it {s} vbytes of block space.
tx.f.sperrzeit_folgenlos: It carries a locktime, but every one of its sequence numbers is final, which leaves that locktime without effect.
tx.f.sperrzeit_hoehe: It could not become valid before block {h}.
tx.f.teils_weg: {n} of its {gesamt} outputs have already been spent again.
tx.f.teils_weg_1: One of its {gesamt} outputs has already been spent again.
tx.f.unterwegs: {n} outputs are being passed on right now, in transactions that are not confirmed yet.
tx.f.unterwegs_1: One output is being passed on right now, in a transaction that is not confirmed yet.
tx.f.unverbreitet: This node has not handed it on to anyone yet — it probably originated right here.
tx.f.verteilung: It pays {n} recipients at once — that is what a payout batch looks like.
tx.f.verwaist: It sits in a block that is no longer part of the longest chain, so it counts as unconfirmed.
tx.f.wartet: It has been waiting in the mempool for {dauer}.
tx.f.wechselgeld: Output {n} has the same script type as the inputs. Often, though not always, that is the change coming back.
tx.f.wiederverwendung: One output pays back to the very script it just spent from. That links both payments together in public.
tx.f.zu_billig: At {rate} sat/vB it is below what the last {n} blocks have been charging ({min} sat/vB), so it may sit for a long while.
tx.f.zu_viele_eltern: With {n} inputs, looking every predecessor up one by one would put more load on your node than this page is worth. The input amounts therefore stay open.
tx.f.zusammenlegung: It sweeps {n} inputs into a single output — that is tidying up, not paying someone.
tx.locktime.inert: without effect — every input is final
tx.miss.notxid: That is not a transaction ID. A transaction ID is exactly 64 hexadecimal characters long.
tx.miss.notxindex: Your node keeps no transaction index, and this transaction is not waiting in the mempool either. Without that index it can only look up what is currently pending. Add txindex=1 to your bitcoin.conf and let it build once; after that Satscope finds every transaction there has ever been.
tx.miss.title: Transaction not found
tx.miss.unknown: Your node does not know this transaction: it is neither waiting in the mempool nor in any block it holds.
tx.miss.unreachable: Your node did not answer. Nothing can be looked up while it stays silent.
